findings.title: Light-theme color of embedded-post author link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR replaced it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme branch is now 70% lightness instead of the original 30%. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the light-theme value unchanged (e.g. `.names span a` in common/base/topic-post.scss correctly uses 30%/70%). On light themes the bold username link in expanded "in reply to" posts will now render as a very light gray, likely failing contrast and looking washed out. The first argument should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`.

findings.title: Light-theme color of .custom-message-length flipped from 70% to 30% lightness
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme branch changed from 70% lightness (light gray hint text) to 30% (dark gray), while the equivalent rule in desktop/modal.scss was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` keeping 70% for light. The flag-modal custom message length counter will render much darker than intended on light mobile themes, and mobile now contradicts desktop. The arguments appear swapped; the first should be 70% and the second 30%.

findings.title: Light-theme color of mobile .topic-map h3 changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 20% to 50% lightness, and it no longer matches the desktop equivalent, which this same PR converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` in desktop/topic-post.scss. Topic-map headings will be visibly lighter on light mobile themes and inconsistent with desktop. The first argument should remain `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` (paired with 80% on $secondary).

findings.title: Light-theme color of .group-member-info .name silently changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; the PR replaced it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The PR's stated purpose is to add dark-theme variants without altering light-theme rendering, but here the light-theme value moved from 30% to 50% lightness, making group member names noticeably lighter on light themes. If the harmonization with the adjacent `.title` rule (50%) was intentional it should be called out; otherwise the first argument should stay at 30%.

findings.title: Light-theme color of mobile .group-member-info .name silently changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: Same issue as the desktop stylesheet: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch changed from 30% to 50% lightness even though the PR's goal is only to add a dark-theme alternative, so group member names will render lighter than before on light mobile themes. Keep the first argument at 30% unless the visual change is intentional.
